findings.summary: scripts/smoke-cas.ts is not re-run safe, so the gate's mandated second run will fail. After the implementation-time run required by spec §5.2, the entity head is the in_flight revision written by step ②. On the gate re-run, step ① dedupes and returns the same entity_id, then step ② calls claimClue(), which reads that head and short-circuits at src/bus.ts:234-237 because payload.status !== "open", returning error "conflict". The assertion expect(claimed.success).toBe(true) therefore fails deterministically. Step ③ passing in run 1 is precisely what guarantees step ② fails in run 2 — the script's two assertions are mutually exclusive across runs. Spec §5.2 requires the gate re-run to hit deduplicated:true and thereby prove both that the script works and that the idempotency guard holds; the fixed idempotency key only bounds writes, it does not make the assertions state-tolerant. Because gate rejection is terminal (§5.2), this reproduces the exact failure class this re-dispatch exists to prevent.

The A6 same-source-read test has no power against mutation M4 (spec §6: "把 casUpdateClue 的 supersedes 改成来自第二次独立读的 head"). The stubbed fetch returns the identical openHead object for every /entities/ request, so a mutant that performs a second independent read before publishing would still produce supersedes === "msg_001" and the assertion on line 78 would still pass. Killing M4 requires the second /entities/ read to return an advanced head with a different message_id while asserting supersedes still equals the first read's message_id. As written, the test satisfies the literal recipe in §4 A6 but does not deliver the mutual-exclusion guarantee §6 attributes to it, leaving the invariant that the whole package exists to protect unguarded.

Spec §5.2 makes it a hard requirement to paste the actual output of the one real smoke run (the three steps' message_id and channel_seq) into IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY or the commit message. No IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY file exists anywhere in the subject worktree, and no run output appears in any tracked product or protocol file, so the required evidence that the script has touched reality is not verifiable from the delivered tree. Given that the previous dispatch died precisely because the smoke script reached reality for the first time at the gate, this evidence cannot be treated as optional.

The tautological A2 case was removed from test/cas.test.ts but relocated verbatim into test/bus.test.ts rather than deleted or rewritten. Spec §4 A10 names it as passing under both the old and new implementations (the old includes("409") lived only in the catch branch, which an HTTP 200 never enters) and heads the requirement "不留恒真断言". Moving it preserves a check that cannot fail; §4's A2 row is already satisfied by the discriminating M1 case immediately below it at lines 65-78.

tsconfig.json's include is ["src", "test"], so scripts/smoke-cas.ts is outside the scope of `npm run typecheck`. The script relies on an unchecked structural cast to PublishWithEntity because PublishResponse (src/bus.ts:70-74) does not declare entity_id. This is consistent with the frozen-file boundary in spec §3 and is not itself a defect, but it means the one deliverable that must survive a real bus call receives no static verification.
